name: agent-layout
title: Agent Layout
description: The shell of an agent MINI-APP (an app.json miniApps item with `agent`): a conversations sidebar (the agent's persona, New chat, the mini-app's own pages, the live conversation index grouped by source Chats / Workflows / Feedback, each row marked with its status by shape, with filters + rename, the signed-in user's menu) beside the route content, rendered by the mini-app folder's layout.tsx with nothing around it. AgentConversation is the conversation page (the empty new chat at new.tsx, one thread at threads/[threadId].tsx; index.tsx is a plain redirect — to the work board, or to new for an agent with no work items); the URL is the source of truth for the selected conversation. A block (AgentLayout) composed from exported parts (AgentLayoutRoot with its `sidebar` slot / Sidebar / Persona / Nav / NewChat / NavLink / Conversations / UserMenu) for mini-apps that need a different sidebar. Over the mini-app's pages, sidebar picks open the conversation in the app's FLOATING AGENT CHAT (FloatingAgentChatProvider once in the layout that wraps the whole app; without it, picks navigate) — built in. Never hand-build thread lists or chat UI around agents.
docs: Load the agent-mini-apps skill — it is the contract for an agent mini-app's folder (layout.tsx, index.tsx, new.tsx, threads/, the mini-app's pages); this note only names the parts. AgentLayout (props: agentChat, links, userMenuItems, chatContext, private — show each signed-in user only their own conversations; a display filter, not access control) is the mini-app's shell — render it in routes/<agent>/layout.tsx as the ENTIRE route element with <Outlet /> inside, agentChat={useAgentChat(<Agent>ChatAgentChat)} (the mini-app's own agent-chat block); it carries the persona, every conversation anyone had with its agent (whichever chat block it went through), the nav (New chat, then `links`) and the user menu itself. index.tsx is a plain <Navigate replace /> — to the work board, or to new for an agent with no work items. AgentConversation (props: threadId, suggestions, placeholder, size, chatContext) renders only in new.tsx (no threadId — the empty new chat, the only place suggestions belong) and threads/[threadId].tsx. Its header has a minimize button (md+, with the floating chat): the conversation moves into the floating chat panel, back on the page the panel's expand came from, else on the layout's first link — AgentLayoutRoot's `minimizeTo`, which AgentLayout fills from `links` (a forked composition passes it); nothing to build. A thread URL takes `?runId=<agentRunId>` to open the conversation AT one agent run (its first message scrolled into view, its messages tinted briefly; a run not in the thread opens it normally) — link a row the agent wrote to it with threadHref(basePath, threadId, { runId }) from agent-layout-context, the thread id being the row's createdByAgentThreadId (or a column's updatedByAgentThreadId) and the run id its createdByAgentRunId (or the column's updatedByAgentRunId), both from useEntityAttribution; AgentConversation reads it from the URL, the route file passes nothing extra. AgentConversation ships feedback built in, on the agent's admin chat only and for the agent's admins only (the layout's block with `isAdmin: true`, AND a caller who is an admin of the agent — builders always, else a role in the agent's `adminRoles`, every signed-in user when it is unset; no feedback UI shows otherwise) — thumbs under each assistant turn (Send records the rating only; Add comment sends a normal message about that reply, answered in the same conversation), with no feedback button in the composer; the agent may propose a change to itself on a Remember this rule? card (its text is editable before approving), and an approved change opens a feedback thread (`fb-…`) in the sidebar under Feedback, with a `Feedback · From …` line above its transcript — never hand-build thumbs or feedback forms. AgentViewport frames a lone AgentChatSimple (over its own agent-chat block) for people who don't get the layout. `new` and `threads` are reserved segments. SIGNED-IN USERS ONLY — the layout throws for an anonymous visitor; anything narrower is the app's own decision in layout.tsx (useUser() role/permission), like any layout. One agent-chat handle per surface, all from the brief's AGENTS line; never hand the layout's handle to AgentChatSimple. Sidebar picks on the mini-app's pages open the app's floating agent chat (FloatingAgentChatProvider once in the layout that wraps the whole app, added with this item; without it, picks navigate); a page's own control: useAgentLayout().openConversation({ chatThreadId }). Give the provider `agents` — one entry per agent mini-app ({ agent: <Name>Agent, agentChat: <Name>ChatAgentChat, entryRoute: the mini-app's app.json entryRoute }) — and the platform's rail (the chat bubble on an agent's row) opens a new chat with any of them in the floating chat panel.

changelog.description: Imports the chat from agent-chat.tsx (deep-agent-chat.tsx is gone with agent-chat 2.0.0) and no longer refuses an agent by its harness — every agent runs on the one chat.

The full conversation page (AgentConversation) gets a minimize button at md+: it moves the conversation into the floating chat panel and goes back to the page the panel's expand came from, else to the layout's first link (AgentLayoutRoot's new minimizeTo prop, which AgentLayout fills; a forked composition passes it). The layout also folds this agent's floating chat whenever it is up over the agent's own conversation page, the panel the platform's app rail opens included; a new chat folds into the page's composer, which takes focus. Re-install the item's files; nothing else to do.
Imports `logOut` from `@blocksdiy/blocks-client-sdk/reactSdk`, where the platform helpers live. Nothing changes in behaviour.
Thread links no longer carry ?chatId= (old links still open their thread); new private prop shows only the current user's threads (a filter, not access control).
A sidebar pick that opens the new chat in the floating panel names the mini-app's new-chat route, so the panel's expand shows before the first send.
Adds the floating agent chat and prompt; the chat files come from the `agent-chat` item it installs.
changelog.migration: Mount `FloatingAgentChatProvider` with its `agents` once in the app-wide layout, per the item's docs.
